title: The Harvard Computers classify the stars
summary: Generations of women at Harvard College Observatory measured and classified stars on photographic plates, building the star catalogues astronomy still uses.
why: Their classifications became the standard system for stars.

notes.problem: Source: 'some of Pickering's female staff were astronomy graduates', not 'many'.

unsung.contribution: Processed and classified hundreds of thousands of stellar spectra from photographic plates.
unsung.recognition: Some were astronomy graduates, yet they were paid like unskilled workers, with little chance of promotion.
